Checked the actual expression trees for 1/B, beta and 1-beta, first-iteration branch, t*B+j, positive-singular-value inverse and subtraction by eta. They match Algorithm 1 and the norm definitions term for term.

One primitive call obtains one sample. The partial-batch branch makes no point update; the completed-batch branch makes exactly one source update and records W_(t+1). Later execution lemmas must establish T*B calls.

The raw algorithm has no random selector: it uses Unit with Dirac law. Randomness comes from sampleOracle tape law P; the later oracle model requires the source IID unbiased finite-variance assumptions. No independence was inferred from P alone.

This internal source unit exports no public result and no complexity statement. The raw stored-trajectory output remains available to analytic proofs, while point-output accuracy will be separately implemented and reviewed.

EuclideanSpace on matrix entries gives the Frobenius geometry; singular values from the Gram matrix define nuclear norm, and the Euclidean linear-map norm defines spectral norm. Compact rather than full SVD prevents arbitrary null-space motion.
